headline: The University of Texas System is setting up a $25 million, state-funded program to oversee and develop the AI tools used in its hospitals and medical schools, but has shared few details.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: a regional but large program, with details drawn from internal documents.
importance_line: Patients, staff and students at Texas's large public hospitals and medical schools are affected, along with AI vendors, but the plan's details come from internal documents and its leaders did not answer questions.
summary: The Houston Chronicle reports, citing internal documents, that the University of Texas System's UT REAL program would keep a record of every AI tool used at its eight medical schools and hospitals (571 uses were counted), watch them for harm and fund promising ones. One outside AI expert quoted by the paper asks whether patient data will be collected and how problems would be handled, and the program's leaders did not answer questions.
notes: Details come from internal UT documents and open-records requests; UT REAL leaders did not respond to the Chronicle.
